police-officer.definition: A person outside the police who enforces rules and preserves order within a group or classroom.

detective.definition: A police officer who investigates crimes.

sergeant.definition: Any of several noncommissioned officer ranks in the Army or Air Force or Marines ranking above a corporal.

chief.definition: The person in charge of a police department or group.

dispatcher.definition: The official who signals the beginning of a race or competition.

k9-officer.definition: A person who holds a position of authority in an organisation, especially the police or military.

patrol-officer.definition: A police officer who regularly checks a designated area, prevents crime, enforces the law, and handles emergencies.

forensic-analyst.definition: A specialist who examines scientific evidence related to investigations and prepares findings for legal use.
forensic-analyst.exampleUsage: The forensic analyst documented the laboratory findings.

traffic-officer.definition: A police or enforcement officer who helps manage road traffic and enforce traffic laws.
traffic-officer.exampleUsage: The traffic officer directed vehicles around the closed road.

undercover.definition: Conducted with or marked by hidden aims or methods.

badge.definition: Any feature that is regarded as a sign of status (a particular power or quality or rank).

handcuffs.definition: To confine or restrain with or as if with manacles or handcuffs.

radio.definition: To transmit messages via radio waves.

baton.definition: A thin tapered rod used by a conductor to lead an orchestra or choir.

vest.definition: A collarless men's undergarment for the upper part of the body.

body-camera.definition: A small wearable camera used to record events from an officer's viewpoint.
body-camera.exampleUsage: The officer checked the body camera according to department policy.

taser.definition: Using a conducted-energy weapon, such as a Taser, to temporarily incapacitate or immobilize someone with an electric discharge.

pepper-spray.definition: A nonlethal aerosol spray made from oleoresin capsicum, a hot-pepper extract, can temporarily blind and disable an attacker and deter bears.

whistle.definition: A small object blown to make a loud signal.

patrol-car.definition: A police car used by officers who patrol streets and communicate with their headquarters by radio.

motorcycle.definition: A two-wheeled motor vehicle ridden by one or two people.

helicopter.definition: An aircraft without wings that obtains its lift from the rotation of overhead blades.

van.definition: (Great Britain) a closed railroad car that carries baggage or freight.

bicycle.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle moved by pedalling.

boat.definition: A small vessel used for traveling on water.

suv.definition: A high-performance four-wheel drive car built on a truck chassis.

k9-unit.definition: Unit 731 was a covert Japanese Army organization based in occupied Manchuria during World War II. It developed biological weapons, conducted experiments on human beings, and committed severe atrocities.

undercover-car.definition: A police vehicle that has limited or no obvious external markings identifying it as a police car.
undercover-car.exampleUsage: The training diagram labels an undercover car as an unmarked police vehicle.

ambulance.definition: A vehicle that takes people to and from hospitals.

front-desk.definition: A service desk near a building’s entrance where visitors register, ask questions, or request assistance.

holding-cell.definition: A secure room in a police station, courthouse, jail, or similar facility holds people for a limited time. They may be waiting for questioning, processing, transfer, or a court appearance.

interrogation-room.definition: A controlled room used by law-enforcement personnel to conduct formal questioning during an investigation.
interrogation-room.exampleUsage: The legal lesson discusses safeguards that apply during questioning.

evidence-room.definition: A secure room where collected evidence is stored, tracked, and protected.
evidence-room.exampleUsage: The evidence room requires authorized access.

locker-room.definition: A room in a sports facility or workplace where people change clothes and leave personal belongings in lockers.

dispatch-center.definition: A communication center that receives calls and sends police or emergency units to incidents.
dispatch-center.exampleUsage: The dispatch center sent officers to the reported location.

parking-lot.definition: An area with marked spaces where vehicles can be parked.
parking-lot.exampleUsage: Police vehicles were parked in the station parking lot.

break-room.definition: A room where staff can rest or eat during scheduled breaks.
break-room.exampleUsage: Officers used the break room between assignments.

training-room.definition: A room used for classes, briefings, or professional training.
training-room.exampleUsage: The department held a safety briefing in the training room.

report.definition: A written evaluation of a student's scholarship and deportment.

warrant.definition: A writ from a court commanding police to perform specified acts.

fingerprint.definition: A print made by an impression of the ridges in the skin of a finger.

mugshot.definition: A photograph of someone's face (especially one made for police records).

evidence-bag.definition: A specialized bag or package used to contain and label evidence while preserving its documented handling history.
evidence-bag.exampleUsage: The sealed evidence bag carried an identifying label.

case-file.definition: A group of records about one legal matter, stored together for people to consult and assess.

id-card.definition: A card containing information used to identify an authorized person.
id-card.exampleUsage: Staff displayed an official ID card.

pen.definition: A writing implement with a point from which ink flows.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer was used during the activity.

crosswalk.definition: A marked place where people cross a road safely.

traffic-light.definition: The light’s current color tells drivers whether they may proceed, should use caution, or must stop.

speed-limit.definition: The highest speed at which motor vehicles may lawfully travel on a particular road or within a designated area, as set by signs or traffic law.

stop-sign.definition: A red, eight-sided road sign requires drivers to halt before crossing an intersection.

siren.definition: A sea nymph (part woman and part bird) supposed to lure sailors to destruction on the rocks where the nymphs lived.
siren.exampleUsage: The siren was identified during the lesson.

barrier.definition: Any condition that makes it difficult to make progress or to achieve an objective.

cone.definition: A visual receptor cell in the retina that is sensitive to bright light and to color.

caution-tape.definition: Bright tape used to mark an unsafe area.

camera.definition: Equipment for taking photographs (usually consisting of a lightproof box with a lens at one end and light-sensitive film at the other).

alarm.definition: To fill with apprehension or alarm.
